about.1:
A “no” that is part of an ambivalent game with the simultaneous presence of an affirmation and a negation, from which no overcoming can arise. The possible becomes reality, in the sense in which Bergson enunciated it, where the possible is not a ghost waiting for its moment to assume a real, concrete form. On the contrary, the possible is reality.
Mercedez Replinger, from the book Instalações Barja - 2005, text “A linguagem do olhar”.
TO BE OR NOT TO BE TO GULLAR*
*Ferreira Gullar is a Brazilian poet and art critic [Translator’s note]

Mercedez Replinger, extract from Instalações Barja - 2005 / “The language of seeing”/MARISA FLORIDO .

trecho.2: series of Brazilian and European theoreticians and artists: Evgene Bavcar, Mercedes Replinger, Adolfo Montejo Navas, Roland Campos, Angélica Madeira, Bené Fonteles and Marília Panitz produced an important set of reflections that accompany this compilation of records that survived time. It is possible, in this way, to traverse here twenty years of history through the projects and installations: “Experiência Tumulto (1985)”, “Cubo Cruz Lápide (1985)”, “O Profeta e a Jaguatirica (1985-86)”, “DO AKD-MICO AO POLE-MICO (1986)”, “Mognus Dei (1990)”, “O Sol de Goethe (1999)”, “São João Beuys (1990)”, “Ser ou não Ser, Ao Gullar (1993)”, “Pega Manet/De Onde Vem A Escuridão (1986)”, “TV Anal (1999)”, “Hermógenes (1999)”, “Obranome (2003)” and “Cultura X Natureza = Barbárie (1998/2005)” Marília Panitz, in her text “Ao que importa, uma resposta”, proposes an itinerary for reading Barja’s works, starting from the concept of equation, so dear to the artist. In the “enigmas of visual equations” of Barja’s commentary-constructions, the author highlights the condensation of meanings that has humour as its tool. Appropriating the sharp steel of irony, armed with a laughter of Oswaldian inspiration, the anthropophagous B
trecho.3: dives into the universe of “Hermógenes” and of “O Sol de Goethe”. Bavcar is interested above all in the white cane, one of the objects that compose “Hermógenes”; it becomes “the invisible canvas, the painting to be created (...) the brush over the darkness”. What Barja paints, in composing the space, is the “difficult path of the invisible”, penetrable, perhaps, by the forms the artist formulates. Mercedes Replinger, together with Marília Panitz, is the one who examines the whole of Wagner Barja’s work. Replinger situates Barja’s work not only in relation to the reflections of contemporary Brazilian criticism, especially Ferreira Gullar, whom Barja brilliantly answers in “Ser ou não Ser. Ao Gullar” (1993), but in what concerns contemporary Western thought. Replinger thus shows how Barja manages to re-pose, in his own manner, questions that pervade the work of John Cage, Georges Bataille, Lezama Lima, Jacques Derrida, Walter Benjamin, Bergson, among others. trecho.4: The eye, without doubt, has a history; it also has a language that incontestably speaks to us. We shall approach the work of Wagner Barja precisely through that gaze, which is a listening, by means of an itinerary traced by some concrete works and installations that, among other themes, interrelate through certain aspects: the problem of the visibility and invisibility of the work, from the metaphors of light to those of blindness; the passage from image and text to the object. Lastly, the explicit homages to his cultural and artistic past, of which he feels himself heir, in conflict. From Ferreira Gullar, Lygia Clark, J. Beuys to Aleijadinho; that is, it follows a trajectory from the avant-gardes to the roots proper to the Brazilian baroque. This division does not imply a strict separation, for all these themes and concepts appear to a greater or lesser degree in each of the pieces and installations, which represent in themselves an excess and a residue that unfolds in the following work and generates a continuous process of metamorphoses, thus underlining the open character of artistic creation. To look, in this sense, necessarily implies theorizing, generating a thought that is constructed with the very movement of the eyes. Co
trecho.5: pertinent to recall the formulation that Ferreira Gullar made in the sixties of the non-object as presence, immanence, absolute transparency. The non-object, according to the critic, renounced the name of things, that is, their opacity: “only through the connotations that the name and use establish between the object and the world of the subject can the object be apprehended and assimilated by the subject. The object is therefore a hybrid being, composed of name and thing… the non-object, on the contrary, is one, integral, frank. The relation it maintains with the subject dispenses with an intermediary. It possesses a signification too, but that signification is immanent to its own form, which is pure significa

From that point on, says the critic, all that remains is to sit upon the rubble and to remain imprisoned in the avant-garde illusion. Ferreira Gullar’s interest is, in reality, more incisive and broader than simple mockery, which dwells on the more superficial aspects of some highly representative artists such as Christo, Vito Acconci or Cris Burden (29), which, on the other hand, is not in a condition to understand itself. What Ferreira Gullar criticizes is, in reality, the very foundation of the new behaviours, incompatible with what, for him, is called the essential nature of art, which is none other than construction and order.
